interest: Illuminates grassroots commercial re-entry under SCAP, Japanese technician travel diplomacy, and legal petitions regarding German repatriates' property.
overview: This file documents the regulation of civilian entry, travel clearance, and commercial activity in occupied Japan from late 1949 to early 1950, alongside an attached 1945 wartime intelligence report on mercury smuggling. Primarily generated by the State Department's Division of Protective Services and the Army's Pacific Military Permit Branch in coordination with SCAP, the records track entry applications for merchants, missionaries, corporate agents, and dependents seeking to revive Japanese foreign commerce. Additionally, the collection details key policy discussions regarding SCAPIN 2035 on sending Japanese technical experts abroad, as well as high-level diplomatic appeals regarding the postwar forced repatriation and property confiscation of German residents.
